recommendations.claim: Google AI features use the same core ranking and quality systems as traditional Search.
recommendations.action: Maintain existing SEO: crawlability, non-commodity content, clear structure.
recommendations.validation: Google's AI features documentation states this explicitly.

recommendations.claim: Content with unique perspective and first-hand experience is more likely to be surfaced in AI features.
recommendations.action: Ensure each tool and guide page contains original explanation or examples not trivially available elsewhere.
recommendations.validation: Google's guidance recommends unique, valuable, non-commodity content.

recommendations.claim: Sites opted out of OAI-SearchBot will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers.
recommendations.action: Ensure robots.txt does not block OAI-SearchBot. This is a deployment policy decision, not a code change.

recommendations.claim: OpenAI may use multiple search providers. The specific index source is not publicly documented.
recommendations.action: Do not assume Bing is the sole index. Submit sitemaps to Bing as an existing external webmaster action; do not treat it as a new GEO implementation.
recommendations.validation: OpenAI does not publicly confirm its index source. Third-party analyses suggest Bing is one provider among possibly others.

recommendations.claim: PerplexityBot surfaces and links websites in search results; Perplexity-User handles user-initiated fetches and generally ignores robots.txt.
recommendations.action: Ensure robots.txt does not block PerplexityBot. Perplexity-User will fetch regardless if a user requests it.
recommendations.validation: Perplexity's official crawler documentation distinguishes the two.

recommendations.claim: Microsoft is introducing independent AI Training and AI Grounding preferences, replacing NoArchive and NoCache. New preferences take effect February 1, 2027; old directives stop being honored March 1, 2027.
recommendations.action: Do not implement new preferences yet. Plan a migration before March 1, 2027. The DisallowExtended directive is Microsoft's opt-out for AI training and AI grounding; adding it to robots.txt (or the equivalent meta tag) prevents Bingbot-sourced content from being used in those contexts. Do not add DisallowExtended until the new preferences are officially live.
recommendations.validation: Microsoft's October 2026 announcement and technical documentation state the dates, the DisallowExtended directive, and the planned retirement of NoArchive/NoCache.

recommendations.claim: Disabling Claude-SearchBot prevents content from being indexed for search optimization.
recommendations.action: Ensure robots.txt does not block Claude-SearchBot if citation visibility is desired.
recommendations.validation: Anthropic's help center documentation distinguishes the three bots.

recommendations.claim: Gemini grounding with Google Search uses the Google Search index and returns citations via groundingMetadata.
recommendations.action: No GEO-specific action beyond Google SEO. Existing Googlebot access and sitemap are sufficient.
recommendations.validation: Gemini API documentation describes grounding with Google Search; Google's common crawlers documentation identifies Googlebot.

recommendations.claim: Meta-WebIndexer improves Meta AI search quality. Allowing it in robots.txt helps Meta cite and link to content in Meta AI responses.
recommendations.action: Ensure robots.txt does not block Meta-WebIndexer if citation visibility is desired. Meta-ExternalAgent covers training and direct indexing; Meta-ExternalFetcher handles user-initiated fetches and may bypass robots.txt.
recommendations.validation: Meta's official web crawlers documentation distinguishes all three.

recommendations.claim: Grok uses live web search and X post search. No robots.txt crawler is documented by xAI.
recommendations.action: No confirmed robots.txt lever. Treat as experimental; do not implement GEO changes based solely on Grok.
recommendations.validation: xAI does not document a robots.txt crawler. Third-party analysis describes web_search and x_search API tools.

recommendations.claim: DeepSeek's search API returns authority (0–4) and rerank_score (0–3) fields for returned pages. These are API output fields, not documented website-ranking criteria.
recommendations.action: Do not assume these fields define DeepSeek's own ranking. Treat as experimental.
recommendations.validation: DeepSeek's API exposes these fields; it does not document how they are computed or whether they reflect website-level ranking.

recommendations.claim: You.com's Answer API returns a synthesized response with a Citations section listing sources by title and URL.
recommendations.action: No confirmed robots.txt crawler or ranking criteria. Treat as experimental.
recommendations.validation: You.com SDK documentation describes answer citations but not crawler behavior or ranking.
